unit.title_en: Getting around by bus and tram
unit.can_do_en: ask which bus or tram goes where and buy a ticket.

brief.situation_en: Maria asks Anna on the bus.

lines.speaker: Maria
lines.gloss_en: Excuse me, is the next stop Kamppi?

judge.reason: Only register differences (anteeks/anteeksi, onks/onko); same question about Kamppi.

lines.speaker: Anna
lines.text_puhe: Ei, Kamppi on vasta kolmas pysäkki.
lines.text_kirja: Ei, Kamppi on vasta kolmas pysäkki.
lines.gloss_en: No, Kamppi is only the third stop.

judge.reason: Okei/selvä, mä oon/minä olen, uus/uusi are register variants; same meaning.

lines.speaker: Anna
lines.gloss_en: No worries. Where are you going?

judge.reason: sä meet/sinä menet are register variants; same question about where you are going.

lines.speaker: Maria
lines.gloss_en: I'm going to the library, Oodi.

judge.reason: mä meen/minä menen; same destination, library Oodi.

lines.speaker: Anna
lines.text_puhe: Sit sä jäät pois Kampis ja kävelet sinne.
lines.text_kirja: Sitten sinä jäät pois Kampissa ja kävelet sinne.
lines.gloss_en: Then you get off at Kamppi and walk there.

judge.reason: sit/sitten, sä/sinä, Kampis/Kampissa are register variants; same content.
onks/onko only register difference; same question.
ihan/aivan and viis minuuttii/viisi minuuttia are register variants; same five minutes.

forms.why_en: Means 'excuse me', a polite way to get someone's attention before asking.

forms.form_name_en: present tense, 3rd person singular, with the question ending -ko/-kö
forms.why_en: Means 'is...?'. The question ending -ko turns 'on' (is) into a question.
Seuraava means next. It comes from seurata, to follow.
This is the dictionary form. People say it the same way.
Ei on its own answers 'no'. People say it the same way.
Means 'is': present tense, 3rd person singular, going with 'Helsinki'.
This is the dictionary form. People say it the same way.
This is the dictionary form. People say it the same way.
Okei is the everyday spoken OK. Books write selvä, which means clear.
Means 'I'. Spoken Finnish often says 'mä'.
Means 'am': present tense, 1st person singular, so it goes with 'minä'. Spoken: 'oon'.
Means 'new', describing Maria herself: 'I am new here'. Spoken: 'uus'.
Means 'here', telling where she is new.
The partitive after ei: ei hätää, no worries.
Mikä with -hin for 'to': mihin, where to.
Means 'you' (one person). Spoken: 'sä'.
Mennä with -t for 'you': menet. Speech says meet.
Mennä, to go, with -n for 'I': menen. Speech says meen.
Kirjasto with -on for 'to, into': kirjastoon.
Oodi with -in for 'to': Oodiin.
An adverb: 'then', the next step. Spoken short as 'sit'.

forms.lemma_meaning_en: to stay (jäädä pois, to get off)
forms.why_en: Jäädä with -t for 'you': jäät. Jäädä pois means to get off.
This is the dictionary form. People say it the same way.
And: joins the coffee and the bun in the order.
Kävellä, to walk, with -t for 'you': kävelet.
Sinne means to there, for moving towards a place.
'It.' Nominative singular, referring back to the price.
Kaukana means far away, at a distance.
Ihan is the everyday spoken word. Books write aivan.
Lähellä means near or close by.
Speech drops the final i: viisi becomes viis.
After a number the noun takes the partitive: kymmenen minuuttia. Speech turns -ia into -ii.
